title: Vanishing of Hom in a transfinite union of subcomplexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $\lambda$ be a limit ordinal, and let $(K_\beta^\bullet)_{\beta<\lambda}$ be a continuous increasing system of subcomplexes (cochain complexes as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]) with monomorphic transition maps and colimit $K_\lambda^\bullet$. Let $I^\bullet$ be a cochain complex whose every term is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. If $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(K_\beta^\bullet[n],I^\bullet)=0$ for every $\beta<\lambda$ and every $n\in\mathbb Z$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(K_\lambda^\bullet[n],I^\bullet)=0$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.

source.place: Lemma lemma-characterize-K-injective, proof at the limit step (Homology Lemma homology-lemma-ML-over-ordinals)

proof.text: For a complex $K^\bullet$ write $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ for the complex of abelian groups with $\operatorname{Hom}^n(K^\bullet,I^\bullet)=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(K^j,I^{j+n})$ and differential $d(f)=d_I\circ f-(-1)^nf\circ d_K$. With the shift convention $(K[1])^r=K^{r+1}$, differential $-d_K$, of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], a degree-$n$ cocycle is exactly a chain map $K^\bullet[-n]\to I^\bullet$ and the degree-$n$ coboundaries are exactly the null-homotopic ones, so $H^n(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K^\bullet,I^\bullet))=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(K^\bullet[-n],I^\bullet)$. Since $n$ ranges over all of $\mathbb Z$, the hypothesis says precisely that each $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K_\beta^\bullet,I^\bullet)$, $\beta<\lambda$, is acyclic. Colimits of complexes are computed termwise and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(-,I^{j+n})$ turns colimits into limits, so $K_\lambda^\bullet=\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\lambda}K_\beta^\bullet$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K_\lambda^\bullet,I^\bullet)=\varprojlim_{\beta<\lambda}\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K_\beta^\bullet,I^\bullet)$. For $\beta<\lambda$ and every $n$, $\varprojlim_{\gamma<\beta}\operatorname{Hom}^n(K_\gamma^\bullet,I^\bullet)=\operatorname{Hom}^n(\operatorname{colim}_{\gamma<\beta}K_\gamma^\bullet,I^\bullet)$, and the map $\operatorname{colim}_{\gamma<\beta}K_\gamma^\bullet\to K_\beta^\bullet$ is a monomorphism (zero for $\beta=0$, the transition map $K_\gamma^\bullet\to K_{\gamma+1}^\bullet$ for $\beta=\gamma+1$, an isomorphism by continuity for $\beta$ a limit); since each $I^{j+n}$ is injective, restriction along it is surjective termwise, so $\operatorname{Hom}^n(K_\beta^\bullet,I^\bullet)\to\varprojlim_{\gamma<\beta}\operatorname{Hom}^n(K_\gamma^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ is surjective (a product of surjections).

source.place: Lemma lemma-characterize-K-injective, proof at the limit step; Homology Lemma Tag 0AAT (lemma-ML-over-ordinals) hypotheses

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-ML-ordinals] with $\alpha=\lambda$ to the inverse system $(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K_\beta^\bullet,I^\bullet))_{\beta<\lambda}$, whose hypotheses (acyclicity and termwise surjectivity onto the earlier limits) were checked in the previous step. Its conclusion makes $\varprojlim_{\beta<\lambda}\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K_\beta^\bullet,I^\bullet)=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K_\lambda^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ acyclic, so $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(K_\lambda^\bullet[-n],I^\bullet)=H^n(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K_\lambda^\bullet,I^\bullet))=0$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$, which is the conclusion.
